solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wound Tarzan up, regularly missing mother

indicators.note: regularly missing means every other letter is skipped, keeping the first, third, fifth and seventh

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Tarzan gets worked up because his mother keeps disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is the noun for an injury, not the past tense of wind; 'up' is part of the letters picked from.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is the medical term for a physical injury or wound, as well as for emotional shock.

clue.text: Cruel to imprison thus and shoot foreign friend from Iraq area

indicators.note: to imprison something is to hold it inside, so the cruel word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a cruel person is mean
so means thus, in this way
to pot is to shoot, as a ball in snooker or game with a gun
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A brutal regime locks someone up and guns down an overseas pal somewhere near Baghdad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' is the snooker sense, to pot a ball, and 'foreign friend' is the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, lies largely within modern Iraq, so the adjective describes that region.

clue.text: Accepting Farah possibly raced, made rough notes

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the rest
rough means unrefined or disordered, so the letters of made are mixed up

parts.note: Mo Farah is a British Olympic distance runner, so Mo is one example
to have raced is to have run

explanation.surface: Mo Farah's race is scribbled down in rough jottings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' makes MEDA from 'made'; 'possibly' marks Mo as one Farah among others, the British Olympic distance runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda is the Latin plural of memorandum, written notes made as reminders or records.

clue.text: Fixed a problem with radio reception

definitions.meaning: fixed in the sense of unmoving, stationary
crackling interference from atmospheric electricity on a broadcast

explanation.surface: A repair man boasts he has sorted out the wireless signal trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, and it is also the noun for crackling electrical noise disrupting radio signals.

clue.text: Tricky performer's piano support that is enjoyed by me before a Glastonbury feature

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: before means coming earlier, so these pieces precede the final ones

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a rest is a support, as for an arm or a cue
said by the one enjoying it this is I dig it, dig being slang for like
Glastonbury Tor is the hill overlooking the Somerset town famous for its music festival

explanation.surface: A festival-goer enthuses about a piano stand and a magician at Glastonbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like i.e., but it is IT in the phrase I DIG IT. Glastonbury Tor is a conical hill in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror whose sleight of hand fools the audience, a performer of tricks.

clue.text: Desperate character about to stop recording moving performance

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the recording

parts.note: a tape is a recording
Desperate Dan is the burly cowboy in the British comic The Dandy
c is the abbreviation for circa, about

explanation.surface: A frantic person is poised to halt a recording of an emotional show.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a long-running character in the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dance is a performance in which the dancer's feet keep moving, with metal plates beating rhythms.

clue.text: Instant expression of impatience for the Scottish wander

parts.note: a mo is an instant, as in just a mo

parts.words: expression of impatience for the Scottish
parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation of impatience or annoyance

explanation.surface: A Scot tuts in a moment of impatience at someone ambling about.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander about aimlessly or loiter in a listless way.

clue.text: Two ways to mature, but not with contemporaries?

definitions.note: plural people defined by a singular group noun; the question mark flags the looseness

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the with letter is taken away

parts.note: to age and to grow up are two ways of maturing

explanation.surface: A musing on two ways of growing older, minus companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE and GROW UP together lose their W.
explanation.definitionFit: People born around the same time form a cohort, a band of peers counted together in surveys.

clue.text: An element of bourgeois desire

indicators.note: an element is one constituent part, so a run of consecutive letters inside the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A sly remark that wanting things is part of middle-class nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an urge is a strong desire or impulse to do something.

clue.text: One's worked for life's ultimate complex polymer

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the last letter of the word life is used
complex means intricate or tangled, signalling the letters of polymer are mixed up

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about a polymer that is the end-point of life's complexity.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'polymer', rearranged, give MPLOYER after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The one for whom you have worked is your boss, the firm or person who pays your wages.

clue.text: Baggy shorts in parcel carried by sweet son

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: sweet in the sense of endearing, cute
a lot is a parcel, as of land or goods at auction
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A doting parent's lad brings home a package containing roomy short trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Culottes are women's knee-length trousers cut very full so they hang like a skirt.

clue.text: Stick instruction in layout of classifieds?

definitions.meaning: to stick is to cling or hold fast
split in two, the word is what a page designer might write: place the advert in this spot

explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface; read as AD HERE it is a layout instruction for a small advert.

clue.text: Judge initially at sea, swallowing murderer's story of seaside crime

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letters of both judge and at are taken
swallowing takes something inside, so the murderer goes into the sea word

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
Cain, who killed his brother Abel in Genesis, is the first murderer

explanation.surface: A judge lost at sea encounters a killer, reading like a coastal thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' tempts as an anagram signal, but 'initially' takes A from 'at' and 'sea' is the poetic main.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's novel of that title tells of Cornish wreckers luring ships to destruction on the coast.

clue.text: Transatlantic counterpart of Co. (UK) providing text collection

parts.note: Americans abbreviate a company as Corp., for corporation, where Britons write Co.
the transatlantic counterpart of the UK is the US

explanation.surface: A business-jargon gloss on how British company names translate in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transatlantic counterpart' covers both Co. and UK: each is swapped for its American equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpus is a body of writings or texts gathered together, as for linguistic study.

clue.text: Toughen control to benefit Anglicans

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as on a horse
for means in favour of, as in all for it
CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A church reformer's plan to tighten discipline for the good of the Anglicans.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to strengthen it, making it tougher with extra support.

clue.text: Provide too little equipment for a pit's description

definitions.meaning: to arm too little, supplying insufficient weapons
the armpit lies beneath the arm, so this word describes its position

explanation.surface: A mining complaint that a colliery has been short of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pit' looks like a coal mine; it is the armpit.
explanation.definitionFit: Under-arm means to give too few weapons, and as an adjective it names the armpit area.

clue.text: Corrupt European leaves tropical disease reduced by last quarter

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the European letter is taken out
the final quarter of an eight-letter word is its last two letters, which are dropped

parts.note: beriberi is a tropical disease caused by lack of thiamine

explanation.surface: A medical note on a European escaping a tropical illness that is waning.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last quarter leaves BERIBE; removing the first E gives the answer. 'Corrupt' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To bribe someone is to corrupt them by offering money or favours for dishonest help.

clue.text: Set out to get into beer, say, and start to see dots

indicators.note: to get into is to enter, so the rearranged letters go inside the beer word

parts.note: beer is an example of a brew

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters of set are shuffled
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone getting stuck into beer starts seeing spots before the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges 'Set' to EST. 'dots' is a verb here, meaning scatters, not spots seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To dot a surface is to scatter things over it, which is exactly what bestrewing means.

clue.text: Spoke with hostility to listeners, to make unwelcome advances

indicators.note: what listeners hear is the sound of a word, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to inveigh is to speak or write with hostility against something

explanation.surface: Someone harangues an audience and then pushes unwanted attentions on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To invade is to make hostile advances into territory that is not welcome to receive you.

clue.text: Cunning about self-identified feminists, good in a smooth way

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cunning word goes round the rest

parts.note: a cunning person is sly
wimmin is a spelling some feminists adopted to avoid the word men

explanation.surface: A wily operator circles a group of feminists, and things go well.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go swimmingly go easily and without hitches, as smoothly as a swimmer gliding.

clue.text: Note inversion of flying creature's major vein

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: an inversion turns something upside down, which in a down answer means reading the word backwards

parts.note: a bird is a flying creature

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that a flying creature's main blood vessel is upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The midrib is the central vein running along a leaf, its largest one.

clue.text: Sponge dessert with fruit served up that's lovely

indicators.note: served up in a down answer means turned upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of puréed fruit folded into cream
ah is an exclamation of pleasure

explanation.surface: A diner sighs with delight as a fruity dessert is brought out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a classic British pudding, such as gooseberry fool. 'Sponge' looks like a cake; it is the bath scrubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous inside of a gourd, used like a sponge for scrubbing in the bath.

clue.text: Heavy object's width against small cube

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: against means next to or touching, so the two parts are placed side by side

parts.note: eight is two cubed, a small cube number

explanation.surface: A furniture-mover sizes up a heavy block by measuring it against a little cube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cube' is a number here: 8 is the cube of 2.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy object, such as one used on scales, as a paperweight or in a gym.

clue.text: Give a reflective look, a steady one, taking in lake

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the lake letter goes within

parts.note: a gaze is a steady look, the one referring back to look
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone stares thoughtfully and steadily out over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' suggests thinking, but it means shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To glaze a surface is to coat it with a glassy layer so that it shines and reflects light.

clue.text: Soviet leader's fall, within a month

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: within means inside, so the fall word goes into the rest

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A historical note that a Soviet leader was toppled within a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Andropov, formerly KGB chief, led the Soviet Union from 1982 until his death in 1984.

clue.text: Bird with an inclination to interrupt one that's domesticated?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a pet is a tame animal kept at home
an gives A, the indefinite article
a rake is a slope or inclination, as of a stage

explanation.surface: A bird keen to butt in on the household's tame animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small, long-tailed parrot, often kept as a caged pet.

clue.text: Attempt to manipulate by following fuel cut

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the by letter goes at the end
cut means shortened, so the last letter of the fuel word is dropped

parts.note: coal is a fuel
X stands for by, as in 2 by 4 written 2x4

explanation.surface: Someone tries to manoeuvre a decision after the fuel supply is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' gives X through the multiplication sign used in measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to try to persuade or steer someone gently, working on them with flattery.

clue.text: Edition of album with reams in that is very big

indicators.note: an edition is a version put together anew, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A deluxe album release comes padded with reams of extra material.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBUM, REAMS and IE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great to be measured is vast, so the word serves as a stronger form of huge.
